title: Quiz: History of the Periodic Table

questions.stem: What was the key contribution of Dmitri Mendeleev to the periodic table?

options.text: He proved that atoms were indivisible
He discovered the first element
He discovered electrons
He arranged elements by atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered elements

questions.explanation: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of atomic mass and grouped them by similar properties. He left gaps for elements he predicted would be discovered later, and his predictions proved remarkably accurate.

questions.stem: What did Newlands propose with his 'Law of Octaves'?

options.text: That elements should be arranged by colour
That there were only eight elements
That atoms contain eight protons
That every eighth element had similar properties when arranged by atomic mass

questions.explanation: Newlands noticed that every eighth element showed similar properties when arranged by atomic mass, like notes in a musical octave. However, this pattern broke down for heavier elements.

questions.stem: Why were early attempts to classify elements incomplete?

options.text: Scientists could not measure the mass of elements
There were too many elements to organise
Not all elements had been discovered, and atomic structure was not yet understood
Scientists did not believe in atoms

questions.explanation: Many elements had not yet been discovered, and without knowledge of protons and atomic number, scientists could only use atomic mass, which sometimes gave incorrect orderings.

questions.stem: Why did Mendeleev sometimes swap the order of elements in his table?

options.text: He did not know the correct atomic masses
He made mistakes in his calculations
He prioritised grouping elements with similar chemical properties over strict atomic mass order
He wanted to make the table look neater

questions.explanation: Mendeleev swapped certain elements (like tellurium and iodine) because their chemical properties did not match the groups they would fall in based purely on atomic mass. This showed his insight into periodic patterns.

questions.stem: How are elements arranged in the modern periodic table?

options.text: In order of discovery
In order of increasing atomic number (number of protons)
In order of increasing atomic mass
In alphabetical order

questions.explanation: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number (number of protons), which solved the problems with Mendeleev's mass-based arrangement.

questions.stem: What evidence proved that Mendeleev's periodic table was correct?

options.text: Other scientists agreed with him immediately
He discovered new elements himself
Elements he predicted were later discovered with properties matching his predictions
He won a Nobel Prize

questions.explanation: Mendeleev predicted the properties of undiscovered elements (like 'eka-silicon', later discovered as germanium). When these elements were found and matched his predictions, his table was validated.

questions.stem: Which discovery explained why elements in the same group have similar chemical properties?

options.text: The understanding of electronic structure and outer shell electrons
The discovery of radioactivity
The discovery of neutrons
The discovery of isotopes

questions.explanation: The discovery of electronic structure revealed that elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, which is why they show similar chemical properties.
